description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of three audio-based models — Qwen2-Audio-Instruct, Audio-Reasoner, and Qwen2.5-Omni — on the MMAR benchmark, specifically evaluating their accuracy when processing audio versus noise inputs, with a baseline for random choice also shown. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 0% to 60% with tick marks at 10% intervals. The horizontal axis lists the three models, each represented by two adjacent bars: a solid blue bar for “Audio” input and a solid purple bar for “Noise” input, with a light blue dashed horizontal line indicating the “Random Choice” baseline at approximately 30%. For Qwen2-Audio-Instruct, the audio input achieves ~30% accuracy while noise input drops to ~23%. Audio-Reasoner shows higher performance with audio at ~37% and noise at ~30%. Qwen2.5-Omni significantly outperforms the others, reaching ~57% with audio and ~36% with noise. The chart visually emphasizes that all models perform better on audio than noise, and Qwen2.5-Omni substantially exceeds the random baseline and other models in both conditions.
